answer: At the marketplace inlet, every agent must lock a bond of 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding for work. Creating identities along a branching vine earns no free access: each new account needs its own bond. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize 100,000 tokens, paying financing costs and forgoing other returns. The nectar of extra identities becomes less attractive because access scales with committed capital.
